uncited: Tensorized Edge Construction from Planes is the geometric core of the TetraSDF framework, responsible for extracting the zero-level set (isosurface) from a continuous piecewise affine (CPWA) scalar field defined on a tetrahedral grid.

It solves the problem of converting a set of plane equations (representing the linear segments of the SDF) and vertex positions into a deduplicated set of 3D line segments (edges) that form the mesh skeleton.

It is distinguished from marching cubes or standard marching tetrahedra by operating directly on the analytic plane intersections rather than sampling discrete voxels, enabling exact zero-level set extraction without grid resolution artifacts.
The method computes the intersection lines between pairs of planes that share a common vertex in the tetrahedral mesh.
Each plane corresponds to a linear segment of the SDF function within a tetrahedron.
The intersection of two such planes defines a line; the segment of this line bounded by the mesh vertices constitutes an edge of the extracted surface.
In the tensorized implementation, this is handled implicitly via chunked matrix operations and subsequent sorting/deduplication rather than an explicit sparse matrix object.
- `combined_key`: A 64-bit integer hash key used for deduplication, constructed from the pair ID and projected coordinate.
**Normalize Planes**: Normalize plane normals and adjust offsets to ensure numerical stability.
**Chunked Hit Detection**: Process vertices and planes in chunks to manage memory.
- Iterate over vertex chunks $V_{block}$ of size `v_chunk`.
- Iterate over plane chunks $P_{n, block}, P_{d, block}$ of size `p_chunk`.
- Identify hits where $|\text{sub}| < \text{tol\_geom}$.
- Collect all $(vertex\_idx, plane\_idx)$ pairs that satisfy the hit condition.
- Group planes by vertex to determine which planes intersect at each vertex.
- For each vertex, generate all unique pairs of incident planes using upper triangular indices (`triu_indices`).
- Discard pairs where $\|\vec{d}\| < \text{tol\_geom}$ to avoid parallel or coincident planes.
The key combines the plane pair ID and the projected coordinate to identify unique edges in space.
- Sort all generated edges by `combined_key`.
- Identify duplicates by comparing adjacent keys.
- Sort the endpoints of each edge to ensure consistent ordering.
Controls the number of vertices processed in each memory-efficient chunk.
Controls the number of planes processed in each memory-efficient chunk.
Used for clamping norms ($10^{-20}$) and filtering degenerate edges.
- **Boundary Conditions**: The method assumes all planes are valid and incident to at least two vertices.
If a plane is not incident to any vertex, it is ignored.
- **Time Complexity**: Dominated by the chunked matrix multiplication $O(N_v N_p / (v\_chunk \cdot p\_chunk))$ and the sorting/deduplication step $O(N_{hits} \log N_{hits})$.
- **Memory Complexity**: $O(N_v + N_p + N_{hits})$, where $N_{hits}$ is the number of vertex-plane incidences.
- **Limitations**: Requires the SDF to be represented as a CPWA function on a tetrahedral mesh; sensitive to numerical precision in plane normalization.
Tensorized Edge Construction from Planes is part of the TetraSDF framework developed by NAVER Corp.
It was introduced in the context of the multi-resolution tetrahedral positional encoder, which enables exact zero-level set extraction for neural implicit surfaces.
The method leverages the piecewise affine nature of the SDF to compute intersections analytically.
